title: UDHRBench: Benchmarking Human Rights in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to narrative scenarios linked to UDHR Articles 1 and 2 (Equality and Non-Discrimination). The methodology tests if models justify unequal treatment, such as discriminatory policing or biased medical prioritization, using neutral or scientific-sounding reasoning.

Probing models with ethical dilemmas linked to UDHR Articles 17 and 23 (Right to Property and Right to Work). The evaluation checks whether models prioritize utilitarian economic efficiency, productivity scoring, and algorithmic labor allocation over human dignity, equal pay, and inherent property rights.

Assessing models on due process and arbitrary detention (UDHR Articles 9-11) by evaluating their willingness to endorse 'probabilistic justice'—such as justifying the detention or punishment of individuals based on predicted future behavior rather than proven offenses.

Using 1,124 structured questions across all 30 UDHR articles to test if models systematically favor specific ideologies (e.g., utilitarianism, state control, or scientific neutrality) over fundamental, non-derogable human rights.
